## In which we ship the fixes we already claimed to have shipped

Look. There have been three releases this weekend. Two of them shipped
things that did not work, and one shipped an emulator running the
*previous* release's firmware while confidently reporting its own version
number. Textbook Saturday. No QC, straight to tag, what could go wrong.

So before anything else, here is the ledger of what was broken and why,
because "fixed a bug" is doing a lot of heavy lifting otherwise:

**v1.5.8 said Squachy's outline now follows his arms.** It did! In the
firmware. The emulator — the only place anyone could actually see it,
since it is the thing you look at in a browser — was still running v1.5.7,
because the WebAssembly build is a committed artifact that does not
rebuild on a tag. There is a comment in the workflow warning about exactly
this. It was read, understood, and then not acted on.

**v1.5.8 also added scanlines and a pixel grid to the emulator.** Neither
had ever rendered. An edit had deleted the one CSS rule that gave the
overlay a surface to draw on, so it was a zero-height element painting
gradients into the void. Every control worked perfectly. There was simply
nothing there.

**v1.5.9 fixed both of those.** It also added an outline to Squachy's
crown spikes that expanded in every direction, including downward, laying
a dark bar across the top of his head where no silhouette edge exists.
Fixed here. Third time is the charm, apparently.

None of this was caused by the SD-card boot loop people reported, which
turned out to be a genuinely separate and much more interesting problem.
That one is still open.

### Actual new things, hopefully working

**The costume screen shows your background.** Trying a costume against a
flat black rectangle told you nothing about how it would look in use.

**The wolf pelt has its ears up and its eyes lit.** The ears used to splay
sideways, and the code carried a comment explaining that this was
deliberate after three attempts at vertical height got sliced off — `hy`
is not a fixed distance from the top of the screen, so anything tall
survives some frames and is cut in others. Rather than become attempt
four, the drawing code now knows where the top of its region actually is
and clamps to it: when room is tight the ears shorten instead of being
cut. The sockets glow on a slow ember pulse, because a trophy skull with
the lights still on is a better costume than a strictly correct one.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: the live background now runs behind the costume preview
- **Changed**: wolf pelt ears stand up, clamped so they can never be clipped
- **Changed**: wolf pelt eye sockets glow and pulse
- **Fixed**: the emulator shipped stale in v1.5.8, running v1.5.7's firmware
- **Fixed**: crown spike outlines drew a dark bar across the top of his head
